Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The Sabbath is mentioned in several passages; the draft states each as worded and does not decide how the transformation of 2:65 and 7:166 is to be understood.

## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about those who broke the Sabbath. None is used in this draft.
- Wording a scholar should check first: 2:65 and 7:166 (be apes, despised), 4:47 (the curse of the Companions of the Sabbath and its addressees), 16:124, 7:164 (who speaks to whom).
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Ayla, Eilat and other names given to the town of 7:163; none is used.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The Sabbath and the test  (`#the-sabbath-and-the-test`)

Cited ayat: 4:154, 7:163, 16:124

> **4:154** وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَهُمُ ٱلطُّورَ بِمِيثَٰقِهِمْ وَقُلْنَا لَهُمُ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْبَابَ سُجَّدًا وَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ لَا تَعْدُوا۟ فِى ٱلسَّبْتِ وَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُم مِّيثَٰقًا غَلِيظًا

> **7:163** وَسْـَٔلْهُمْ عَنِ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلَّتِى كَانَتْ حَاضِرَةَ ٱلْبَحْرِ إِذْ يَعْدُونَ فِى ٱلسَّبْتِ إِذْ تَأْتِيهِمْ حِيتَانُهُمْ يَوْمَ سَبْتِهِمْ شُرَّعًا وَيَوْمَ لَا يَسْبِتُونَ لَا تَأْتِيهِمْ كَذَٰلِكَ نَبْلُوهُم بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَفْسُقُونَ

> **16:124** إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ ٱلسَّبْتُ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخْتَلَفُوا۟ فِيهِ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا۟ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (4:154): God raised the Tur above them for their covenant, told them to enter the gate prostrating, told them not to transgress in the Sabbath, and took from them a firm covenant.

**c2** (7:163): The one addressed is told to ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the Sabbath.

**c3** (7:163): On the day of their Sabbath their fish came to them openly, and on the day when they did not keep the Sabbath the fish did not come.

**c4** (7:163): The ayah says that in this way God tested them because of their disobedience.

**c5** (16:124): The Quran says that the Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it, and that your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection about what they differed in.

### One-minute summary

God told them not to transgress in the Sabbath [c1]. The fish came to them openly on the day of their Sabbath and did not come on other days, and the Quran says that God was testing them [c3][c4].

### Complete story

God raised the Tur above them for their covenant, told them to enter the gate prostrating, told them not to transgress in the Sabbath, and took from them a firm covenant [c1]. The one addressed is told to ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the Sabbath [c2]. On the day of their Sabbath their fish came to them openly, and on the day when they did not keep the Sabbath the fish did not come [c3]. The ayah says that in this way God tested them because of their disobedience [c4]. The Quran says that the Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it, and that your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection about what they differed in [c5].

### Deep study

- God raised the Tur above them for their covenant, told them to enter the gate prostrating, told them not to transgress in the Sabbath, and took from them a firm covenant (4:154) [c1].
- The one addressed is told to ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the Sabbath (7:163) [c2].
- On the day of their Sabbath their fish came to them openly, and on the day when they did not keep the Sabbath the fish did not come (7:163) [c3].
- The ayah says that in this way God tested them because of their disobedience (7:163) [c4].
- The Quran says that the Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it, and that your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection about what they differed in (16:124) [c5].

### Kids mode

God told them not to break the Sabbath [c1]. The fish came to them only on the day of their Sabbath, as a test [c3][c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage sets a command beside a test that made keeping it hard [c1][c3][c4]. One reading is that the ayat treat the test as something that shows what people do [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: where the town by the sea was, when this happened, or how many lived in it; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: the one addressed in 7:163 is not named in the ayah.
- Not established: what the differing about the Sabbath in 16:124 refers to is read in more than one way.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the town and the sea; none is used here.

## 2. A community that warned  (`#a-community-that-warned`)

Cited ayat: 7:164-165

> **7:164** وَإِذْ قَالَتْ أُمَّةٌ مِّنْهُمْ لِمَ تَعِظُونَ قَوْمًا ٱللَّهُ مُهْلِكُهُمْ أَوْ مُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا قَالُوا۟ مَعْذِرَةً إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ وَلَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ
>
> **7:165** فَلَمَّا نَسُوا۟ مَا ذُكِّرُوا۟ بِهِۦٓ أَنجَيْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ ٱلسُّوٓءِ وَأَخَذْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ بِعَذَابٍۭ بَـِٔيسٍۭ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَفْسُقُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (7:164): A community among them asked others why they admonished a people whom God was going to destroy or punish severely.

**c2** (7:164): The others answered that it was an excuse before their Lord, and that perhaps the people would fear God.

**c3** (7:165): When the people forgot what they had been reminded of, God saved those who forbade evil.

**c4** (7:165): God seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment because of their disobedience.

### One-minute summary

Within the town, a community asked why others admonished a people God would punish, and the others said that it was an excuse before their Lord [c1][c2]. God saved those who forbade evil and seized those who did wrong [c3][c4].

### Complete story

A community among them asked others why they admonished a people whom God was going to destroy or punish severely [c1]. The others answered that it was an excuse before their Lord, and that perhaps the people would fear God [c2]. When the people forgot what they had been reminded of, God saved those who forbade evil [c3]. God seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment because of their disobedience [c4].

### Deep study

- A community among them asked others why they admonished a people whom God was going to destroy or punish severely (7:164) [c1].
- The others answered that it was an excuse before their Lord, and that perhaps the people would fear God (7:164) [c2].
- When the people forgot what they had been reminded of, God saved those who forbade evil (7:165) [c3].
- God seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment because of their disobedience (7:165) [c4].

### Kids mode

Some people in the town kept warning the others [c1][c2]. When the others forgot the warning, God saved those who had forbidden what was wrong [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage records people who kept warning, giving as their reason an excuse before their Lord and the hope that the others might fear God [c2]. One reading is that the ayat place the saving of the warners beside the seizing of those who did wrong [c3][c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the ayat do not say how many were in each community, who they were, or how the saving happened.
- Not established: the ayat do not say whether the community that questioned the warners belonged to those who were saved or seized; the draft does not decide.
- Not established: the sense of the excuse before your Lord is read in more than one way.

## 3. The outcome  (`#the-outcome`)

Cited ayat: 2:65-66, 4:47, 7:166

> **2:65** وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱعْتَدَوْا۟ مِنكُمْ فِى ٱلسَّبْتِ فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا۟ قِرَدَةً خَٰسِـِٔينَ
>
> **2:66** فَجَعَلْنَٰهَا نَكَٰلًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَمَا خَلْفَهَا وَمَوْعِظَةً لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ

> **4:47** يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ ءَامِنُوا۟ بِمَا نَزَّلْنَا مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا مَعَكُم مِّن قَبْلِ أَن نَّطْمِسَ وُجُوهًا فَنَرُدَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَدْبَارِهَآ أَوْ نَلْعَنَهُمْ كَمَا لَعَنَّآ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلسَّبْتِ وَكَانَ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفْعُولًا

> **7:166** فَلَمَّا عَتَوْا۟ عَن مَّا نُهُوا۟ عَنْهُ قُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا۟ قِرَدَةً خَٰسِـِٔينَ

### Claims

**c1** (2:65): The Quran says that they knew those among them who transgressed in the Sabbath, and that God said to them: be apes, despised.

**c2** (7:166): Another ayah says that when they exceeded what they had been forbidden, God said to them: be apes, despised.

**c3** (2:66): God made it a deterrent for those before it and those after it, and an admonition for those who fear Him.

**c4** (4:47): The Quran mentions that God cursed the Companions of the Sabbath, in a warning to those who were given the Book.

### One-minute summary

The Quran says that God said to those who transgressed in the Sabbath: be apes, despised, and made this a deterrent and an admonition for those who fear Him [c1][c3]. It also mentions that God cursed the Companions of the Sabbath [c4].

### Complete story

The Quran says that they knew those among them who transgressed in the Sabbath, and that God said to them: be apes, despised [c1]. Another ayah says that when they exceeded what they had been forbidden, God said to them: be apes, despised [c2]. God made it a deterrent for those before it and those after it, and an admonition for those who fear Him [c3]. The Quran mentions that God cursed the Companions of the Sabbath, in a warning to those who were given the Book [c4].

### Deep study

- The Quran says that they knew those among them who transgressed in the Sabbath, and that God said to them: be apes, despised (2:65) [c1].
- Another ayah says that when they exceeded what they had been forbidden, God said to them: be apes, despised (7:166) [c2].
- God made it a deterrent for those before it and those after it, and an admonition for those who fear Him (2:66) [c3].
- The Quran mentions that God cursed the Companions of the Sabbath, in a warning to those who were given the Book (4:47) [c4].

### Kids mode

Those who went beyond what they were told, in the Sabbath, were punished [c1][c2]. God made this a lesson for people who fear Him [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat present the outcome as a deterrent and an admonition for those who fear God [c3]. One reading is that the repeated reference to the Sabbath keeps the focus on exceeding what was forbidden [c1][c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: whether the words be apes, despised describe a change of form or a figure is read in more than one way; the draft states the ayat as worded and does not choose.
- Not established: the ayat do not say how many were affected, what happened to them afterwards, or whether the Companions of the Sabbath of 4:47 are the same group as those of 2:65 and 7:166; the draft does not say so.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the town, the number of the transgressors and the length of time they survived; none is used here.
